pvwatts_system_loss_pct.rationale: Percent system losses passed to PVWatts per shading level. 14% is the PVWatts default; 20% and 30% are product choices for some and heavy shading, not measured values.

target_offset.rationale: Share of annual usage the recommended system aims to cover. Product choice: size to roughly 90-100% of usage.

system_size_cap_kw.rationale: Upper limit on recommended system size so very large bills do not produce unrealistic rooftop systems. Product choice.

panel_degradation_per_year.rationale: Annual loss in panel output used in the 25-year projection. Product choice (0.5% per year).

analysis_years.rationale: Length of the net-savings projection. Product choice (typical panel warranty length).

ca_self_consumption_share.rationale: Share of solar output used on site (valued at the retail rate) versus exported at the lower net billing credit, for California homes. Placeholder product choices pending owner review; batteries raise self-consumption.

annual_rate_escalation.rationale: Yearly growth in the retail electricity rate used in the 25-year projection. Product choices, not sourced facts. Florida: no primary source gives a forward forecast, so 2/3/4% is a choice around general inflation; for context EIA reports a Florida residential average of 14.14 cents/kWh in 2024 (eia.gov/electricity/sales_revenue_price/pdf/table_5A.pdf). California: the Public Advocates Office (CPUC) Q2 2026 Electric Rates Report, page 8, prints residential average rate increases from January 2016 to June 2026 of +69% (PG&E), +101% (SCE) and +97% (SDG&E); over those 10.5 years that is about 5.1%, 6.9% and 6.7% a year compounded (our arithmetic: total^(1/10.5) - 1). The CPUC's 2025 SB 695 report (cpuc.ca.gov, 2025-sb-695-report_093025.pdf, page 6) separately prints simple-average figures of about 11%, 8% and 7% a year for 2016-2024 and a 2025-2028 forecast of about 6-7% a year; it defines these as simple averages, not compound rates. The California range of 3/4.5/6% is deliberately at or below the recent compound history because assuming it persists for 25 years is not defensible. Owner to review.
